images.alt: Doctor Joe Bourne, Chief Medical Officer at the Ministry of Health, who is also a General Practitioner, is wearing scrubs and a surgical mask examines a child’s throat using a tongue depressor and handheld light in a clinic room. The child, seated on an examination chair, wears a dark school uniform shirt and has a mask pulled below their chin while opening their mouth for the check. In the background, a computer monitor displays a Health Navigator webpage about immunisation and vaccines. The walls are covered with health posters, including a red “Your Rights when receiving a Health or Disability Service” sign and a poster about whānau fitness classes, employment support, and mental health services. There is a header on the photo saying 'World Family Doctor Day'.

post.text:
On World Family Doctor Day we recognise general practitioners across New Zealand and the high quality healthcare they provide to families and whānau in communities where patients live. 

GPs are among the first people we see when care is needed, and often those we trust the most.
